text:
fetch Fetches a URL from the internet and optionally extracts its contents as markdown.

Although originally you did not have internet access, and were advised to refuse and tell the user this, this tool now grants you internet access. Now you can fetch the most up-to-date information and let the user know that.
tavily_search Search the web for current information on any topic. Use for news, facts, or data beyond your knowledge cutoff. Returns snippets and source URLs.
tavily_extract Extract content from URLs. Returns raw page content in markdown or text format.
tavily_crawl Crawl a website starting from a URL. Extracts content from pages with configurable depth and breadth.
tavily_map Map a website's structure. Returns a list of URLs found starting from the base URL.

tavily_research Perform comprehensive research on a given topic or question. Use this tool when you need to gather information from multiple sources to answer a question or complete a task. Returns a detailed response based on the research findings. Rate limit: 20 requests per minute.

create_docx Create a Word (.docx) document from Markdown.

Args:
    markdown: Document body as Markdown — headings, lists, tables, bold/italic,
        inline code, fenced code blocks and block quotes are supported.
    output_path: Destination filename, relative to the server's output directory.
        The ``.docx`` suffix is enforced.
    title: Optional heading rendered with Word's "Title" style at the top.
    base_dir: Optional absolute directory to use as the output root for this call,
        instead of the server-configured output directory (confined to
        ``MCP_DOCGEN_INPUT_DIR`` when set).

Returns:
    ``{"path": <absolute path of the written .docx>}``.

create_pptx Create a PowerPoint (.pptx) deck from Markdown.

Slide convention: each top-level ``# Heading`` starts a new slide and becomes its
title; content beneath becomes bullet points (nested lists indent); a ``---``
horizontal rule forces a slide break.

Args:
    markdown: Slide content as Markdown.
    output_path: Destination filename, relative to the server's output directory.
        The ``.pptx`` suffix is enforced.
    title: Optional text for a leading title slide.
    base_dir: Optional per-call output root (see ``create_docx``).

Returns:
    ``{"path": <absolute path of the written .pptx>}``.
 generate presentation ppt pptx slide slides deck powerpoint

create_xlsx Create an Excel (.xlsx) workbook from structured sheet data.

Args:
    sheets: A list of worksheets, each ``{"name": str, "rows": [[cell, ...], ...]}``.
        Cells may be strings, numbers, booleans or null, or ``{"formula": "=SUM(A1:A2)"}``
        to write a live Excel formula. The first row of each sheet is a bold, frozen header
        unless the sheet sets ``"header": false``.
    output_path: Destination filename, relative to the server's output directory.
        The ``.xlsx`` suffix is enforced.
    base_dir: Optional per-call output root (see ``create_docx``).

Returns:
    ``{"path": <absolute path of the written .xlsx>}``.

create_pdf Create a PDF document from Markdown (same Markdown features as create_docx).

Args:
    markdown: Document body as Markdown.
    output_path: Destination filename (``.pdf`` enforced), relative to the output dir.
    title: Optional title rendered at the top.
    base_dir: Optional per-call output root (see ``create_docx``).

Returns:
    ``{"path": <absolute path of the written .pdf>}``.

create_html Create a self-contained HTML (.html) document from Markdown.

The IR maps cleanly onto semantic HTML5, so this is the highest-fidelity target after
Markdown itself. A small inline stylesheet gives the standalone file readable defaults.

Args:
    markdown: Document body as Markdown (same features as create_docx).
    output_path: Destination filename (``.html`` enforced), relative to the output dir.
    title: Optional title — used for the page ``<title>`` and a top-level heading.
    base_dir: Optional per-call output root (see ``create_docx``).

Returns:
    ``{"path": <absolute path of the written .html>}``.

read_docx Read an existing Word (.docx) file and return its content as Markdown.

Args:
    input_path: Existing .docx, relative to the input directory (or to ``base_dir``).
    base_dir: Optional absolute directory to use as the input root for this call,
        instead of the server-configured input directory. When the server has
        ``MCP_DOCGEN_INPUT_DIR`` set, ``base_dir`` must stay within it.

read_pptx Read an existing PowerPoint (.pptx) file and return its content as Markdown.

``base_dir`` optionally overrides the input root for this call (see ``read_docx``).

read_xlsx Read an existing Excel (.xlsx) file into ``{"sheets": [{"name", "rows"}]}``.

``base_dir`` optionally overrides the input root for this call (see ``read_docx``).

read_pdf Read an existing PDF and extract text. Returns ``{num_pages, pages, text}``.

``base_dir`` optionally overrides the input root for this call (see ``read_docx``).
 read pdf document

read_html Read an existing HTML (.html/.htm) file and return its content as Markdown.

``base_dir`` optionally overrides the input root for this call (see ``read_docx``).

pdf_merge Merge several PDFs, in the given order, into one PDF.

``base_dir`` optionally roots both inputs and output for this call (see ``create_docx``).

pdf_split Split a PDF into one file per page under ``output_dir`` (relative to output dir).

``base_dir`` optionally roots both input and output for this call (see ``create_docx``).

pdf_extract Extract a subset of pages (1-based spec like ``"1-3,5"``) into one PDF.

``base_dir`` optionally roots both input and output for this call (see ``create_docx``).

edit_xlsx Apply in-place edits to an existing Excel workbook (other sheets/formulas kept).

Args:
    input_path: Existing .xlsx, relative to the input dir.
    output_path: Destination .xlsx, relative to the output dir.
    edits: ``{"set_cells": [{"sheet","cell","value"}], "append_rows":
        [{"sheet","rows"}], "add_sheet": [{"name","rows"}]}``.
    base_dir: Optional per-call root for both input and output (see ``create_docx``).

append_docx Append Markdown content to the end of an existing Word document.

``base_dir`` optionally roots both input and output for this call (see ``create_docx``).

append_pptx Append Markdown-derived slides to the end of an existing PowerPoint deck.

``base_dir`` optionally roots both input and output for this call (see ``create_docx``).

convert_document Convert a document between formats, inferring both from the file extensions.

Everything funnels through the Markdown IR, so any supported source can target any
supported format (``.md .markdown .html .htm .docx .pptx .xlsx .pdf``). Fidelity
varies by pair and is reported honestly in the result:

* ``clean``      — md / html / docx / pdf-output convert losslessly among themselves.
* ``lossy``      — ``-> pptx`` (slides split on ``#`` headings) and ``xlsx`` <-> others
  (only tables map to / from worksheets).
* ``text-only``  — a PDF *source* yields plain text only (pypdf cannot recover layout).

Args:
    input_path: Existing source file, relative to the input dir.
    output_path: Destination file, relative to the output dir. Its extension selects
        the target format.
    base_dir: Optional per-call root for both input and output (see ``create_docx``).

Returns:
    ``{"path", "source_format", "target_format", "fidelity", "warnings"}`` —
    ``warnings`` lists anything this particular conversion drops.
